claude_initial_call: WEAKEST: the end state itself is undefined

audit.primary_source_citation: Gill S, Vasey AE, De Souza A, Baker J, Smith AT, Kohrt HE, Florek M, Gibbs KD Jr, Tate K, Ritchie DS, Negrin RS. "Rapid development of exhaustion and down-regulation of eomesodermin limit the antitumor activity of adoptively transferred murine natural killer cells." Blood. 2012 Jun 14;119(24):5758-68. PMID 22544698; PMCID PMC3382935; DOI 10.1182/blood-2012-03-415364. This is the ORIGIN paper for the named state — its own abstract says "These results provide the first demonstration of NK-cell exhaustion." It is a primary research paper, not a review. (The most-cited secondary framing, Bi & Tian, "NK Cell Exhaustion," Front Immunol 2017;8:760, PMID 28702032 / PMC5487399, is a REVIEW and was explicitly excluded as the primary source under A.1, though it is quoted below as an admission against interest.)

audit.species: Mouse (C57BL/6 and BALB/c donors/recipients; congenic CD45.1; FVB; Rag2-/-Il2rg-/-; NKG2D-/-; DTR-FOXP3-eGFP), plus one xenograft arm using human NK cells in CB.17-SCID recipients bearing human Raji lymphoma. Counter-evidence spans mouse and human.
audit.what_was_measured: In mice, congenically marked CD45.1+ CD3-DX5+ / CD3-NK1.1+ splenic NK cells, DX5-bead-enriched then sorted to >98% purity, were adoptively transferred at 0.5-1.0x10^6 cells/mouse into irradiated CD45.2+ recipients across five models (BALB/c + A20 lymphoma syngeneic; BALB/c + A20 with allogeneic NK; C57BL/6 + Hoxa9-Meis1 AML; subcutaneous tumour with delayed transfer; CB.17-SCID + human Raji with human NK cells). At days 1, 5, 10, 14-17 and 26 post-transfer, donor cells were re-identified by CD45.1 flow cytometry and scored for surface NKG2D / NK1.1 / NKp46 / CD49b, maturation markers CD27 / CD11b / KLRG1, intracellular Eomesodermin and T-bet, IFN-gamma after PMA/ionomycin restimulation, CD107a degranulation, and 51Cr-release cytotoxicity; a forced-Eomes-overexpression arm tested partial rescue. n = 3-5 mice per group per timepoint, 2-3 independent experiments. Critically for this claim: NO inhibitory/checkpoint receptor panel defining a destination state was reported (PD-1 was looked at and reported negative as "data not shown"; TIM-3, LAG-3 and TIGIT were not measured), NO chromatin or DNA-methylation assay was performed, NO clonal or barcode tracking was used, and no antigen-specific stimulus exists for NK cells. The readout is therefore a population-level DECLINE in effector markers and function in traced donor cells over time — a direction of change — not arrival at any independently defined "exhausted NK" cell.
audit.n: 3-5 mice per group per timepoint; 2-3 independent experiments per figure panel (figure-legend language: "at least 3 (A-D) or 2 (E) independent experiments with at least 3 mice per group", with variants of 4 and 5 mice per group). NOT donors or clones — no clonal resolution at all.
audit.controls: Freshly isolated naive splenic NK cells (day-0 input reference); IL-2-activated cultured NK cells; non-tumour-bearing irradiated recipients (isolating tumour exposure from homeostatic proliferation/lymphopenia); transwell cultures to test soluble-factor mediation; NKG2D-/- donor NK cells; Treg-depletion (DTR-FOXP3-eGFP) arm to exclude Treg-mediated suppression; forced Eomes overexpression as a gain-of-function rescue. Congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 marking is the identity control that makes this a transfer observation rather than a snapshot comparison. MISSING controls that bear directly on this claim: no comparator of transferred vs. host-endogenous NK at the same timepoint under identical proliferative load; no clonal/barcode tracking to separate per-cell conversion from differential survival; no independent definition of the end state against which arrival could be scored.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Three alternatives, in increasing order of damage. (1) THE END STATE IS NOT A STATE — the primary alternative. Gill et al. state verbatim: "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology." The destination B is constituted by an analogy, not by an observation. If "exhausted NK" just means "an NK cell whose IFN-gamma/cytotoxicity is lower than an arbitrary comparator (usually autologous blood NK)", then "NK -> exhausted NK" is not a lineage transition at all; it is a restatement of a functional measurement with an arrow drawn through it, and no fate question is being answered. Bi & Tian's own pro-exhaustion review concedes "the transcriptional factors specific for exhausted NK cells are yet to be defined"; Judge/Murphy/Canter state "there is no established NK phenotype for these dysfunctional states" and "there remains controversy as to whether NK cells even undergo exhaustion (as opposed to other dysfunction processes), and if so, the phenotypic markers that define an exhausted NK cell." (2) SELECTION, NOT CONVERSION (the canonical alternative, and it fully survives this design). Donor NK cells were transferred as a bulk polyclonal pool into IRRADIATED, lymphopenic hosts and underwent homeostatic proliferation; the paper itself reports that loss of cytotoxicity "progresses with homeostatic proliferation and tumor exposure." Without clonal or barcode tracking, preferential survival and outgrowth of the already-hypofunctional, terminally mature fraction of the input pool (CD27-CD11b+, KLRG1-high) reproduces every observed population-level fall — mean NKG2D, mean Eomes, mean IFN-gamma, mean lysis — with zero individual cells converting. Congenic CD45.1 marking proves the cells are donor-derived; it does not prove they are the same cells that were functional on day 1. Proliferation-coupled decline is exactly what a selection model predicts, so the paper's own kinetic argument cuts against it. (3) TECHNICAL ARTEFACT in the human literature that built the end state after 2012: the flagship marker PD-1 is either not expressed by NK cells at all (Judge 2020) or is physically stolen from tumour cells (Hasim 2022), and enzymatic tumour dissociation with collagenase/dispase is known to cleave lymphocyte surface molecules, so "intratumoural NK have lost their receptors" can be a digestion artefact.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is unusually decisive because it attacks the DEFINITION of B rather than the transition. (a) Judge SJ et al., J Clin Invest 2020;130(6):3051-3068 (PMID 32134744, PMC7260004, archived): stringent multi-platform assessment (flow, qRT-PCR, RNA-seq) of NK cells from primary human tumours, ex vivo culture, and multiple mouse tumour and viral models — human and mouse NK cells "consistently lack PD-1 expression despite the marked upregulation of other activation/regulatory markers, such as TIGIT," in marked contrast to T cells in the same samples. The prototypical exhaustion marker is absent. (Note: this drew an accompanying commentary, J Clin Invest 2020;130(6):2816-2819, PMID 32391808 — the dispute is live, not settled.) (b) Hasim MS et al., Sci Adv 2022;8(15):eabj3286 (PMID 35417234, PMC9007500, archived full text): Pdcd1-/- NK cells co-cultured with leukemia cells STILL stain positive for PD-1; PD-1 on NK surface "rather than being endogenously expressed, was derived entirely from leukemia cells" via SLAM-receptor-dependent trogocytosis; transwell and actinomycin-D controls exclude soluble transfer and de novo transcription; corroborated in patients with clonal plasma cell disorders, where PD-1+ NK cells co-stain for tumour cell markers. A genetic-knockout control showing the marker is stolen, not induced, is about as strong as artefact evidence gets. (c) THE FOUNDING PAPER ITSELF FAILS THE CANONICAL TEST: Gill 2012 reports it "did not demonstrate increased expression of PD-1, as has been shown for exhausted CD8+ T cells (data not shown)" — the single defining marker of the state it was naming was negative, and was consigned to data not shown. (d) Ndhlovu LC et al., Blood 2012 (PMID 22383801, PMC3335380): TIM-3 "marks human natural killer cell MATURATION" — it is constitutively expressed on healthy mature NK cells, so its later use as an "NK exhaustion marker" (da Silva 2014) is circular. (e) LABEL INSTABILITY WITHIN SINGLE GROUPS: Ardolino et al. classify intratumoural mouse NK cells as "anergic" and reverse it with systemic IL-12/IL-18, while Hsu et al. from the same group describe the same models as PD-1+; Alvarez M et al., JCI Insight 2019 (PMID 31211693) title the state "NK cell exhaustion" while the mechanism they report is the DNA DAMAGE REPAIR pathway — which under T-cell taxonomy is SENESCENCE, not exhaustion. The same cells get three different end-state names. (f) TOX DISANALOGY: in T cells TOX transcriptionally and epigenetically ENFORCES exhaustion (Khan/Alfei/Scott 2019, all cited in Blank 2019). In NK cells TOX is a LINEAGE-SPECIFICATION factor required for the cells to exist — Aliahmad P et al., Nat Immunol 2010 (PMID 20818394), "Shared dependence on the DNA-binding factor TOX for the development of lymphoid tissue-inducer cell and NK cell lineages"; Seehus et al. 2015 (PMID 25915732), TOX-dependent common ILC progenitor. The defining epigenetic driver of the borrowed concept has an incompatible job in the borrowing cell type. (g) NO ANTIGEN RECEPTOR: criterion 1 of the T-cell definition (chronic antigen stimulation through a clonotypic TCR) has no NK counterpart. The closest available substitute, Merino A et al., J Clin Invest 2019;129(9):3770-3785 (PMID 31211698), had to use plate-bound agonistic anti-NKG2C + IL-15 in vitro on human adaptive NK cells — and its own title says "dysfunction and epigenetic reprograming", NOT exhaustion. (h) SEARCHED-AND-NOT-FOUND (G3): I ran five distinct searches for a formal 2019-2024 consensus or nomenclature statement on NK exhaustion or NK dysfunction terminology and located NONE. The nearest thing is the Judge/Murphy/Canter single-group review, not a multi-author consensus. This is a searched negative, NOT a claim that none exists. By contrast the T-cell field's consensus paper was found immediately on the first attempt (Blank CU et al., "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'", Nat Rev Immunol 2019;19(11):665-674, PMID 31570879, PMC7286441, archived).
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCIES. (1) Clinical: the entire NK-directed checkpoint-blockade rationale — monalizumab (anti-NKG2A) and tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) are developed on the premise that a reversible "exhausted NK" state exists and is the thing being reversed; Judge 2020 lists trials already enrolling on the NK-PD-1 premise specifically (NCT03958097, NCT03815084, NCT03937895). If the end state is only a functional decrement rather than an enforced program, "reinvigoration" has no defined target and the biomarker used for patient selection (checkpoint-receptor positivity on NK) is measuring maturation or trogocytosed protein. (2) Dosing schedules for IL-15 agonists: Felices M et al., JCI Insight 2018;3(3):e96219 (PMID 29415897, PMC5821201), "Continuous treatment with IL-15 exhausts human NK cells via a metabolic defect", is the direct justification for intermittent rather than continuous IL-15/N-803 dosing of adoptively transferred NK products. (3) WITHIN THIS SCREEN: X5 sits directly upstream of R2 ("Tumour NK dysfunction reversible vs fixed") — R2 is unanswerable as posed if there is no defined state whose reversibility can be scored; a reversibility experiment needs a B to revert FROM. X5 also underwrites X2 ("Newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK") and supplies the interpretive frame for X4's ENTPD1+ "effector/exhausted" end state and for T4 (NK -> ILC1), where "exhausted" and "converted" are competing labels for the same intratumoural hypofunctional cells. (4) Also load-bearing for CAR-NK product-release criteria, where "exhaustion markers" are used as a QC readout on manufactured cells with no validated definition behind them.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: CONFIRMED on substance, OVERTURNED on grade — and the two point in opposite directions, which is the actual finding. CONFIRMED: the end state genuinely is undefined, and the evidence for that is stronger than the initial call assumed. It is not merely that no one has gotten around to defining it; the founding paper defines it by explicit admission of analogy ("We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology"), the field's own flagship pro-exhaustion review concedes the transcription factors "are yet to be defined", the leading critique states flatly that "there is no established NK phenotype for these dysfunctional states", and a targeted search found no consensus/nomenclature paper of the kind the T-cell field produced in 2019. Applying the T-cell criteria from Blank 2019 (RULE G4), NK "exhaustion" satisfies NONE of them with direct evidence: no clonotypic antigen receptor, so "chronic antigen stimulation" has no counterpart; no demonstrated TCF1+ progenitor -> TCF1- terminal hierarchy; TOX is a developmental requirement in NK cells rather than an exhaustion enforcer; and it is explicitly NOT separated from anergy or senescence — Judge 2020 says the states "become blurred", and Alvarez 2019 labels a DNA-damage-response phenotype "exhaustion" when that is senescence under the T-cell taxonomy. OVERTURNED: "WEAKEST" is wrong as an evidence-design grade, and the initial call would have mis-ranked this row. The founding primary source is NOT marker similarity, an in vitro culture, or a trajectory — it is a congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 adoptive-transfer experiment with longitudinal re-identification of the traced input population across five tumour models, tumour-free controls, a soluble-factor transwell control, a Treg-depletion control, and a gain-of-function Eomes rescue. That is an OBS_TRANSFER design, methodologically stronger than several rows this screen grades ABOVE X5: stronger than S1 (pseudotime only, INF_TRAJECTORY), T3 (in vitro only), T5 (in vitro), X3 and S2 (phenotypic similarity), and X4 (snRNA/snATAC trajectory). So X5 is not the weakest row in the screen on evidence class; it is roughly on par with D2 and T2. THE CORRECTED CHARACTERISATION: X5's defect is SEMANTIC, not METHODOLOGICAL. A competent in vivo transfer experiment was run, and it points at a destination that does not exist. That is a different and more interesting failure mode than "weak evidence", and it should be recorded as its own category rather than collapsed into the bottom of an evidence-quality ranking — because more data of the same kind cannot fix it. No adoptive transfer, parabiosis, barcode or fate-map can establish "A becomes B" while B is constituted by analogy to a different cell type. One further caveat that cuts the other way and is NOT in the initial call: even the strong OBS_TRANSFER design does not exclude the canonical selection alternative, because transfer was bulk and polyclonal into irradiated lymphopenic hosts and decline tracked with homeostatic proliferation — so the row also fails to exclude "a pre-existing hypofunctional subset outgrew the rest."

audit.notes: RULE G4 VERDICT (the hint flagged this as critical): NK "exhaustion" fails every explicit criterion of the T-cell field it borrowed the word from. Blank et al. 2019 (PMID 31570879) is itself a Viewpoint in which 18 experts give differing definitions "ranging from complete lack of effector function to altered functionality", so the source concept is not monolithic — but it does converge on four testable anchors: chronic antigen stimulation, hierarchical progressive functional loss, a TCF1+ self-renewing progenitor feeding a TCF1- terminal population, and TOX-driven epigenetic enforcement distinguishing exhaustion from anergy and senescence. NK cells have no clonotypic antigen receptor (anchor 1 undefined by construction); no NK progenitor-to-terminal exhaustion hierarchy has been demonstrated; TOX in NK cells is a developmental lineage factor (Aliahmad 2010, PMID 20818394) not an exhaustion enforcer; and the anergy/senescence boundary is explicitly unresolved (Judge 2020). The single closest NK study, Merino 2019 (PMID 31211698), is in vitro plate-bound anti-NKG2C + IL-15 on human adaptive NK cells and titles its own finding "dysfunction", not exhaustion. G3 COMPLIANCE: 23 distinct searches were run and read (listed in searches_run). The absence of an NK-exhaustion consensus/nomenclature paper is a SEARCHED negative across five differently-phrased attempts, not an assertion of non-existence; if such a statement exists it is not surfacing under PubMed/EPMC queries for consensus, nomenclature, criteria, misnomer, or critical-appraisal phrasings. Note that the lit.py EPMC backend degrades badly on long natural-language queries (returns conference abstract books); boolean/author-title queries were required. NO HINTED CITATION WAS FOUND TO BE FABRICATED: Wherry, Sharpe, Speiser, Blank consensus on nomenclature = confirmed real and located (PMID 31570879); the 2019-2024 critique literature arguing NK dysfunction is not exhaustion = located, but it is a review (PMID 32117816) plus a primary data paper (PMID 32134744) from one group (Murphy/Canter, UC Davis), not a consensus statement — the hint's framing of "consensus/nomenclature papers" for the NK side overstates what exists. RECOMMENDED ROW DISPOSITION: X5 should be moved out of the evidence-quality ranking entirely and recorded as UNGRADEABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION (destination undefined), with a footnote that its primary source is an OBS_TRANSFER design. Ranking it "weakest" implies that better data would settle it; it would not.
